flagged.location: second paragraph, sentence beginning 'On two-dimensional examples' (line 20): '$|T|=\operatorname{diag}(0,2)$ for the nilpotent Jordan block'
flagged.evidence: The page item ex-square-root-and-absolute-value-of-a-matrix defines T = [[0,2],[0,0]] ('so that Te_1=0 and Te_2=2e_1', T*T = diag(0,4), |T| = diag(0,2)); that T is twice the 2x2 nilpotent Jordan block J = [[0,1],[0,0]] which the batch's counterexamples call 'the Jordan block J' (cex-a-quasinilpotent-operator-need-not-be-zero) and 'the Jordan nilpotent J' (cex-self-adjointness-cannot-be-dropped-from-the-order-calculus), and the page's own next paragraph calls it 'the nonzero Jordan nilpotent'. For the actual Jordan block J one has J*J = diag(0,1), hence |J| = diag(0,1), not diag(0,2); so under the standard (and the page's own) meaning of 'the Jordan block' the sentence attributes to J a computation the page performs only for 2J.
